def is_nested(string):

    Create a function that takes a string as input which contains only square brackets.

    is_nested('[[]]') ➞ True
    is_nested('[]]]]]]][[[[[]') ➞ False
    is_nested('[][]') ➞ False
    is_nested('[]') ➞ False
    is_nested('[[][]]') ➞ True
    is_nested('[[]][[') ➞ True
    '''
\nYour job is to reason through the problem step by step and then create a Python implementation that satisfies the requirements of the docstring. To help with your reasoning, you will be given a Dafny specification, but prioritize the docstring as the Dafny specification could be incorrect. You should just return a single function without the docstring and no added commentary, and make sure to respond with the complete, valid, and idiomatic Python method including the function signature in the following format:\n\n```python\n{YOUR RESPONSE}\n```.
user_prompt:
method is_nested(string: string) returns (result: bool)
    requires string != null
    requires forall i :: 0 <= i < string.Length ==> string[i] == '[' || string[i] == ']'
    ensures result == (exists subsequence: seq<char> :: valid_subsequence(subsequence) && nested(subsequence))

// Helper function to check if the subsequence is valid
predicate valid_subsequence(subsequence: seq<char>)
    ensures |subsequence| % 2 == 0 // Even number of brackets
    ensures forall i :: 0 <= i < |subsequence| ==> (subsequence[i] == '[' || subsequence[i] == ']')

// Helper function to check if there is a nested structure
predicate nested(subsequence: seq<char>)
    ensures exists i, j :: 0 <= i < j < |subsequence| && subsequence[i] == '[' && subsequence[j] == ']' && (j - i) > 1 // At least one bracket in between

    is_nested('[[]]') ➞ True
    is_nested('[]]]]]]][[[[[]') ➞ False

def check(candidate):

    # Check some simple cases
    assert candidate('[[]]') == True, "This prints if this assert fails 1 (good for debugging!)"

    assert candidate('[][]') == False
    assert candidate(('[]')) == False
    assert candidate('[[[[]]]]') == True
    assert candidate('[]]]]]]]]]]') == False
    assert candidate('[][][[]]') == True

    assert candidate('[]]') == False
    assert candidate('[[]][[') == True
    assert candidate('[[][]]') == True
